origin: From the Greek skeuos (vessel, tool) and morphē (shape): imitating the shape and texture of a real object. The leather and wood textures of Apple's apps before iOS 7 in 2013 are classic examples.
whenToUse: Screens that carry over how a real object is used (calculators, recorders).
Explaining new digital concepts through familiar objects.
whenNotToUse: Information-dense work screens (decoration covers the content).
Responsive services across many screen sizes.
Texture images would make loading heavy.
accessibility: Check the contrast of text on textures separately, even after adding shadows.
Announce states in words beyond gloss and pressed looks.
